item.text: {"winner":"A","confidence":"high","summary":"A is closer to the frozen contract because it leaves FilesService.Add unchanged, explicitly validates inputs, and uses the established multipart helper. B’s stronger retry test does not outweigh its deliberate behavioral change to Add.","reasons":["A preserves the existing Add implementation and its lower-level streaming semantics; B changes Add to eagerly io.ReadAll every body, altering memory use, read timing, and reader-error wrapping contrary to the explicit preservation requirement.","A explicitly rejects an empty filename and nil content before encoding or requesting. B delegates these cases implicitly to multipartbody.NewFile, with no visible service-level validation.","Both candidates fail the requirement to route Upload through the existing public Add method: A duplicates Add’s option/request/response logic, while B extracts a private add method and has both entry points bypass that requirement.","B’s Upload retry test is materially better: it uses an open file and verifies multipart field, filename, and content on every attempt. However, B also adds a forbidden Add behavior change and a changelog claim advertising that change."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add’s request construction, option handling, response decoding, and missing-data check, creating drift risk and directly violating the reuse requirement.","The retry test uses strings.NewReader and does not inspect the multipart body on retried requests, so it does not truly verify streamed-content replay.","No added tests visibly cover empty filename, nil content, or source-reader failures."],"risks_b":["Eagerly buffering every Add body changes an existing API’s behavior and can impose unexpected memory costs on callers using custom multipart streams.","Upload calls the new private add helper rather than FilesService.Add, contrary to the specified routing contract.","No added tests visibly cover validation or source-reader errors, and validation is not explicit in Upload itself beyond whatever the helper may do."]}
